Hi Andrew — thanks for the list. We have a concise attestation that addresses each of these items and I attached a working draft (redwood-operator-boundary-attestation-draft.pdf). Key notes up front:

- Operator access: our private deployment package supports a customer-managed bastion (+ optional operator-only jump host) and RBAC that separates operator (systems) vs. tenant/app roles. Operator actions are logged to an audit stream (customer-managed or forwarded to your SIEM).
- Patching & SBOM: we provide an offline patch bundle and SBOM for every release. Patches are signed; customers can validate signatures before applying. We document a staged patch window process for air-gapped installs in §3 of the draft.
- Supply-chain: upstream images and packages are pulled from curated registries; we provide provenance records and tag digests for every release. We also maintain a published 3rd-party dependency list.
- Key management: HSM and customer KMS integrations are supported (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and PKCS#11-compatible HSMs). Keys can be customer-owned; private deployment does not require Redwood-managed key material.
- Cert rotation/rollback: included in the operator runbook (appendix A). We support automated rotation hooks and an emergency rollback that reverts to last-known-good artifacts and revokes compromised certs.

I've looped in Vanessa and Karthik to add technical specifics and any timeline constraints for SOC2 or other compliance evidence. Marissa is copied for legal/contract impacts. Can we sync on a short call tomorrow morning to finalize?

Best,

Andrew / Naomi — adding a few specific clarifications from engineering that we put into the draft and that often come up during customer reviews: 

1) Operator boundary:
- Default deployment ships with operator accounts scoped to a specific cluster/instance. Customer may opt to run operator services within their management VPC or in a separate operator VPC with strict peering rules.
- All operator console access is through a hardened bastion that enforces MFA + certificate pinning. We document session recording and retention options (customer can configure SIEM forwarding or local retention).

2) Offline patching + SBOM handling:
- Patch bundles are released as signed tarballs; signature is FIPS-validated where required.
- SBOM available in SPDX and CycloneDX formats. We provide a verification script that runs in an air-gapped environment to check signatures and digests.

3) Supply-chain provenance:
- We maintain immutable release artifacts (by digest) and an auditable release ledger. For customers requiring additional attestation, we can provide per-release provenance manifests and a summary of build-time controls.

4) HSM/KMS integration:
- Native integrations: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault (transit). PKCS#11 HSMs supported via plugin. Keys can be generated in-customer HSM; Redwood components use a key reference only.

5) Emergency rollback / cert revocation:
- Rollback is a deterministic process defined in the runbook. We include pre-built rollback artifacts and automated hooks that mark prior images/keys as revoked in the local artifact store.

Next steps: Naomi — if the timeline holds, we can update the draft and send the final attestation and an XLS spreadsheet with quick yes/no answers for procurement by EOD Wednesday. Andrew — can you confirm which internal distribution list we should send the final artifacts to? procurement@ or security@?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
